0 Cover Your Assets In Cover Your Assets, players compete to become the first millionaire by building towers of matching sets made from 10 different types of asset cards (things like jewels, piggy banks, classic autos, and more). Each new set that is created is stacked crosswise on top of the previous set, covering, and protecting, all the sets beneath it. The top set of assets in your pile is vulnerable, and can be stolen by other players if they show you a matching asset card, or wild (which are Silver and Gold cards) from their hand. You can defend your stack by showing the challenger a matching card from your own hand. If you do, they can counter with another matching card of their own. The battle rages back and forth until one player can't respond, or bows out. If you win, you keep the set, if the challenger wins, they take the set. Regardless of who wins, ALL the cards used in the challenge are added to the set, increasing its value and allure to other players. To keep the set from being stolen by another player, the best thing you can do is to Cover Your Assets, by creating a new pair from your hand, or by stealing a set from the top of another player's stack during your next turn. At the end of the round scores are tallied, the cards are shuffled, and a new round begins. The first player to reach $1,000,000 wins! [Rating: 1/10] Played this at Blue Highway's light-games marathon. I did not have a good time at all - it seemed like an incredibly swingy form of Rummy with a heavy take-that element. I'm not interested in playing this ever again, but I suppose I could be convinced maybe. If I really liked who I was playing with.

[Rating: 1/10] Terribly designed. You can spend more than half of the game unable to play. The only people who like it are people who don’t know that there are much better games out there.

[Rating: 1/10] No real game here.  Time waster with nearly no decisions to be made.  Randomness plus take that meanness  turns this into an activity far more frustrating than fun.  Don’t waste your time.

[Rating: 1/10] IMHO Box Quote: "I made a funny. Give me your money!"  Make pairs with a hand of four cards. Woo hoo, I'm an idiot. Or steal a pair and have it stolen by someone else randomly. But wait, I made a pair again! In five minutes I might be lucky enough to add up 40 cards!  This random take-that activity only exists to try and justify its titular pun. Why would having a coin collection now protect my stamps? Cover your a$$ets! Get it? Cuz it sounds like ass. Didn't you think I said asses? Ass... ets.  I'm putting Ex-lax in your Metamucil, you dusty old fart. Blow that out your assets.   I hate this 

[Rating: 1.5/10] A twist on go-fish that, even for adults, plays too long. And this is supposed to be for 7+. Skull King was a good twist on a classic card game. This one is not.  Edit: had to play a few more times with extended family; this game is broken. Even a non-gamer at the table commented without my prompting.

[Rating: 2/10] This game is needlessly mean, gives you no ability to build your hand to protect your stack of cards and is completely luck driven. It also has first "set" rule that is completely pointless, whats the benefit of protecting 10-40k in a round that could easily have a winner scoring 600k... I hope, I never have to play this game again. Choose Linko instead, for a game with similar (better) mechanisms and is actually a good game. I wish I could rate this "game" lower.

[Rating: 2/10] [BGCOLOR=#FF3366] [b]2 [/BGCOLOR] Nov 2022 - 1 play[/b] The big money pile decides the game and moves around the table with little control. It’s a bit funny to watch it happen, but pretty miserable to play it out.

[Rating: 2.2/10] I can't find any strategy in this game. I'll play to be social with my family, but if they offer almost ANYTHING else - I will choose the later.
